**Voica v0.6.2 — AI term correction keeps working after Groq retired a model.**

### Fixed

Groq withdrew `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` on **16 August 2026**. That model was the first choice for
**AI term correction** and the one used before the app has ever talked to Groq (first run, or no
network), so correction was aiming at something that no longer exists — costing a failed request
per dictation until the app re-resolved a live model.

The chain is now `openai/gpt-oss-120b` → `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` → `openai/gpt-oss-20b` →
`llama-3.1-8b-instant`. If you had pinned the withdrawn model in Settings, it falls back to
**Recommended (automatic)** by itself.

Dictation was never affected: correction fails open and delivers the original text.

### Added

If Groq refuses the correction model for your organization (**403**), Voica now tells you once per
model per session and names the model, instead of failing quietly — a blocked model cannot fix
itself the way a retired one can. Allow it at console.groq.com → Settings → Limits.

### Install

Two downloads to choose from (Windows 10 1809+ / x64):

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica.exe`** | ~80 MB | nothing — fully self-contained |
| **`Voica-fx.exe`** | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
